title: Sequence-specific 2'MOE antisense oligonucleotides activate human platelets through glycoprotein VI
identifier: PMID 33567808; PMC8804562; DOI 10.3324/haematol.2020.260059 (Haematologica 2022)
required_file: Main text CC-BY PDF from PMC, specifically the per-compound GPVI KD figure/table and the 7-donor GPVI-level-vs-responsiveness correlation panel; plus supplementary methods for donor and blood-draw conditions
gap_closed: Human in vitro assay on five named PS ASOs, three of them clinically dosed 2'MOE compounds, with donor-level variance quantified - the single best human-system record for the phosphorothioate platelet/thrombocytopenia axis
expected_yield: 5 named ASOs (ISIS 487660, ISIS 104838, ISIS 501861, ISIS 120704, ODN 2395) x (GPVI KD, surface P-selectin, platelet-leukocyte aggregate formation); 7 human donors with correlation coefficients r=0.85-0.97; cord-blood megakaryocyte proplatelet arm as a measured negative
found_via: Europe PMC (single resource; no duplicate anywhere in the record set)
caution: VERIFIED CORRECTION - the triage record claims all five bound GPVI at 'KD ~0.2-1.5 mM'. Wrong on units and wrong on uniformity. I read the article: KD is MICROMOLAR and compound-specific (487660 0.2-1.5 uM, 104838 24 uM, 501861 26 uM), with the CpG oligos stronger still. Critically this inverts the naive SAR: 487660 has the highest affinity yet is the compound with no clinical platelet effect, while 104838 and 501861 (24-26 uM) drive SYK-dependent aggregates. Do NOT encode GPVI affinity as a monotonic predictor of clinical phenotype. Endpoint is platelet activation, not clotting time - keep those endpoint families separate.

title: Assessing single-stranded oligonucleotide drug-induced effects in vitro reveals key risk factors for thrombocytopenia (Sewing et al.)
identifier: PMID 29107969; PMC5673186; DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0187574 (PLoS One 2017)
required_file: Main text plus ALL Supporting Information files - the oligonucleotide panel with per-construct length and phosphorothioate linkage counts is the load-bearing table and is not in the abstract
gap_closed: Converts 'phosphorothioates activate platelets' into quantitative per-construct chemistry covariates in a human system: binding and activation scale with oligonucleotide LENGTH and with NUMBER of PS linkages; adds platelet factor 4 as a second target alongside GPVI; LNA wings suppress both
expected_yield: UNKNOWN construct count (panel is in the SI); two continuous chemistry covariates (length, PS linkage number) plus an LNA-wing modification contrast; human platelet binding/activation and human haematopoietic differentiation readouts; assay battery documented for reuse
caution: PS linkage NUMBER is a count, not a position map - this record supports a covariate, not per-position chemistry, so it does not by itself satisfy the position-level requirement. Panel size is UNKNOWN until the SI is opened. Endpoint is thrombocytopenia liability via platelet activation, not clotting-time coagulopathy.

title: Influence of plasma prekallikrein antisense therapy (donidalorsen) on coagulation and fibrinolysis assays: post-hoc analysis
required_file: Table 1 in full, from the CC-BY full text - the Europe PMC record carries NO abstract, so nothing is visible without retrieving the full text
gap_closed: The most complete human coagulation and fibrinolysis panel in the entire record set on a clinically dosed antisense oligonucleotide, with numeric values rather than AE terms
expected_yield: 22 hereditary angioedema patients (donidalorsen 80 mg vs placebo) x 13 named assays x baseline/4-month, each with delta, p-value and reference range: silica aPTT, CAT lag time, peak thrombin, ETP, factor XI activity, prothrombin fragment 1+2, thrombin-antithrombin complexes, HMW kininogen activity, normalised clot lysis time, D-dimer, plasminogen activity, plasmin-alpha2-antiplasmin; median prekallikrein reduction 75% (range 36-94%)
caution: Post-hoc analysis of a phase 2 trial, so not powered for these coagulation endpoints. The aPTT result is a measured NEGATIVE (stayed within reference range) and is mechanistically load-bearing because prekallikrein deficiency itself prolongs aPTT - record it as a measured negative, never as missing data. Ionis co-authorship means sponsor-grade assays but also sponsor-selected reporting.

title: Comparative study of porcine and ovine derived defibrotide: coagulation profiles, molecular characteristics and DNA content
required_file: Full text plus the per-batch data tables: aPTT, thrombin time, amidolytic anti-Xa and anti-IIa per batch; size-exclusion HPLC molecular weight distribution; heparin-red DNA content per batch
gap_closed: The only record that closes a human in vitro assay gap AND tested-material purity/characterisation simultaneously, and it does so at BATCH level - which is what a characterisation column actually needs
expected_yield: 28 API batches (19 porcine, 9 ovine) x 4 coagulation endpoints, approx 112 assay values, plus 28 x (MW, DNA content) characterisation values; ovine 16.8 +/- 0.24 kDa vs porcine 18.02 +/- 0.32 kDa; DNA 75.78 vs 79 ug per 10 ug API; human pooled plasma plus individually analysed healthy-donor whole blood (donor count UNKNOWN)
caution: Authors disclose that NO untreated control samples were included, so every row is uncontrolled against baseline. The headline aPTT result is NEGATIVE (no anticoagulant effect from either source) with only a mild TT effect - valuable as a human negative control, not as a coagulopathy-positive row. Defibrotide is a polydisperse DNA-derived polyelectrolyte with NO single definable sequence: encode as a mixture with an MW distribution and never force a sequence field. Single fixed 100 ug/mL spike, so no concentration-response. The abstract says only 'pooled plasma' - donor-level whole-blood analysis is visible solely in the full text, so this record must not be triaged from its abstract.

title: Platelet activation by antisense oligonucleotides in the Gottingen minipig, with GPVI and PF4 ontogeny
identifier: PMID 37111598; PMC10143489; DOI 10.3390/pharmaceutics15041112 (= OpenAlex W4362470109 = BioStudies S-EPMC10143489)
required_file: Main text Tables 1 and 2 from the CC-BY PDF. Do NOT bother with the supplement (see caution)
gap_closed: The only record giving explicit per-position chemistry - PS positions marked residue-by-residue with asterisks, 2'MOE as uppercase, LNA as underlined uppercase - for 7 constructs, together with a same-construct cross-species platelet map. Isosequential PO (PS load 0) and all-PS variants let backbone be isolated from sugar chemistry
expected_yield: 7 constructs x (per-position marked sequence, length 14-22, PS load 0-21) including ODN2395, ISIS104838 and RTR5001 and their variants; plus 7 constructs x 3 species (minipig in vivo and in vitro, NHP, human) platelet response categories
caution: VERIFIED, resolving a direct conflict between the three triage records (BioStudies called the human arm UNVERIFIED; PubMed asserted a purpose-built bridge matrix). I read the article: Table 2 IS a 3-species table with a Human column covering the same 7 constructs, so the bridge is real - BUT the human and NHP cells are CATEGORICAL literature-collated outcomes (activation / aggregation / no effect), not numeric human assay values. Ingest Table 1 as chemistry and Table 2 as a qualitative concordance map ONLY; it supplies no human numbers. Supplementary Table S1 is merely a juvenile-minipig sample overview from the 8-week tox study, so it carries no human data and is not worth acquiring.

title: Sheehan intrinsic tenase pair: PS oligonucleotides inhibit the intrinsic tenase complex (1998) and do so by an allosteric mechanism (2001)
required_file: Both full-text PDFs via institutional access or interlibrary document delivery - every open publisher route tested has failed
gap_closed: The purified-human-factor mechanism tier, which the dataset most lacks: localises PS aPTT prolongation to the intrinsic tenase (FIXa-FVIIIa) complex, resolves it as hyperbolic mixed-type ALLOSTERIC inhibition rather than nonspecific polyanionic sequestration, and separates a heparin-cofactor-II-mediated component
expected_yield: ISIS 2302 concentration-response in human plasma (PT, TT, aPTT; prolongation above approx 100 ug/mL) plus mechanism-level parameters - Vmax(app) decomposition across complex assembly, cofactor stability and protease catalysis, with controls showing no inhibition of FIXa-phospholipid FX activation and no significant effect on FVIII-phospholipid affinity. Extractable row count UNKNOWN until the full texts are in hand
access: technical_block / confirmed_paywall - four triage records disagree (technical_block, abstract_only, confirmed_paywall). Europe PMC advertises the Blood 1998 full text as 'free after 12 months' at the legacy bloodjournal.org URL, but following the DOI returns HTTP 403 from ashpublications.org
found_via: PubMed + Europe PMC + OpenAlex + Semantic Scholar (8 rows collapsed across the two papers)
caution: This is the single most important PAYWALLED item in the set - spend the document-delivery budget here FIRST, ahead of entries 33 and 42. The mechanism tier matters disproportionately: allosteric and saturable versus polyanionic and concentration-linear changes how the entire dataset should extrapolate aPTT between assay formats and between species. Two papers but one acquisition action, since they are the same construct and the same programme. Do not log as acquired from an abstract. Semantic Scholar indexes the 1998 paper under a legacy Blood locator DOI (10.1182/BLOOD.V92.5.1617.417K13_1617_1625), which is why PubMed-centric queries missed it.

title: Phosphorothioate backbone modifications of nucleotide-based drugs are potent platelet activators (Flierl et al.)
required_file: Main text plus the JEM supplementary material containing the oligonucleotide panel
gap_closed: The mechanistic root node for the whole PS-backbone coagulopathy cluster - attributes platelet activation to the phosphorothioate BACKBONE rather than to sequence or target, and supplies a human genetic negative control in the form of platelets from GPVI function-deficient patients
expected_yield: UNKNOWN panel size (the construct list sits in the supplement); human washed platelet and whole-blood endpoints spanning activation, signalling, ROS, adhesion, spreading, aggregation and in vitro thrombus formation; GPVI-deficient patient arm; paired mouse in vivo thrombus arm
caution: Treat the claimed human-to-animal bridge as UNVERIFIED: the human and mouse arms are in one paper, but construct matching across species must be checked against the methods before this is recorded as a same-construct bridge. Endpoint is platelet activation, not clotting time. It is the reference the Haematologica and Sewing records build on, so expect overlapping constructs - dedupe against entries 1 and 2.

title: IONIS-FXIRx (ISIS 416858) phase 2 in ESRD on haemodialysis - registry results, sponsor protocol and journal supplement
identifier: NCT03358030 (sponsor protocol ISIS 416858-CS5) + PMC8820988 / BioStudies S-EPMC8820988 (Kidney Int Rep 2022) - ONE study, two artifacts
required_file: ClinicalTrials.gov posted-results tables (aPTT percent change, FXI activity percent change, FXI antigen, platelet-count laboratory abnormalities, bleeding) PLUS the 114-page Prot_SAP_000.pdf (Chemistry section; pre-specified aPTT>160 s rule; platelet monitoring rules) PLUS the paper's mmc1.pdf supplement
gap_closed: The richest dose-stratified human aPTT and FXI dataset for a 2'MOE phosphorothioate gapmer anywhere in the set, with exact denominators, alongside the sponsor's own chemistry description and numeric safety thresholds
expected_yield: n=213 across 4 arms (placebo 53, 200 mg 53, 250 mg 54, 300 mg 50); approx 88 aPTT group-by-timepoint datapoints and approx 88 FXI activity datapoints; AE dose gradients with denominators - thrombocytopenia 0/53, 4/53, 6/54, 7/50; platelet count decreased 0/53, 0/53, 4/54, 1/50; AV fistula thrombosis 1/53, 0/53, 2/54, 3/50; epistaxis 1/53, 1/53, 2/54, 5/50; plus serious ITP, cerebral haemorrhage, venous and graft thrombosis
caution: The registry record and the Kidney Int Rep paper are the SAME study - do not enter twice. Registry values are group-level summaries, not participant-level. aPTT is posted as percent change from baseline, so absolute seconds must be reconstructed from baseline values if the model needs them. The supplement's '19 occurrences of MOE' is a raw byte-stream scan, which is not evidence that per-position chemistry is printed inside. Retrieval trap recorded: the literal query 'IONIS-FXIRx' returns 0 hits in BioStudies because subscript markup breaks tokenisation - search 'factor XI antisense' instead.

title: Effects of 2'-MOE antisense oligonucleotides on platelets in human clinical trials, with its cynomolgus platelet-count companion
required_file: Human paper full text and tables from PMC; for the companion, the NHP platelet-count paper full text (currently abstract-only route)
gap_closed: The human DENOMINATOR for the 2'MOE platelet signal across an entire sponsor safety database, and - paired with the companion - a class-level human-to-NHP bridge on platelet count
expected_yield: 2,638 human subjects across 16 distinct 2'MOE ASOs, doses to 624 mg/week, durations to 4.6 years; 7/2,638 (0.3%) with confirmed post-baseline counts between 100 and 50 K/uL; none confirmed below 50 K/uL; 3 of 16 ASOs with >10% incidence of >30% platelet decline; no evidence of altered platelet function including from the FXI ASO trials. Companion adds cynomolgus platelet counts across the same chemistry class (construct count UNKNOWN)
found_via: Europe PMC + Semantic Scholar (2 rows collapsed) plus the separately-listed companion
caution: The central finding argues AGAINST any chemistry-class-level risk term in the model: liability is sequence-specific, not 2'MOE-generic. Compounds are referenced at class level with NO printed sequences, so this cannot serve the chemistry gap at all. The two papers are companions by publication convention, not a matched same-construct design - verify construct overlap before using as a bridge. Subjects overlap with entries 10 and 38 (same Ionis integrated safety database), so dedupe carefully to avoid double-counting.

title: Integrated safety assessment of 2'-MOE chimeric antisense oligonucleotides in non-human primates and healthy human volunteers
required_file: Full text plus the standardised haematology, complement and platelet panel tables
gap_closed: The best class-level animal-to-human extrapolation record available: 12 distinct 2'MOE chimeric constructs under matched dose-ranging designs in BOTH cynomolgus and healthy humans, with explicit statements of where the animal data over-predicts human risk and where NHP correctly predicted safe human doses
expected_yield: 12 constructs x 2 species x standardised haematology, complement and platelet panels
caution: Matched DESIGNS are not necessarily matched doses, matched timepoints or matched assay laboratories - check per-construct dose alignment before computing any quantitative species ratio. Complement is an adjacent, not a coagulation, endpoint. Same author group and same safety database as entries 9 and 38; dedupe subjects and constructs.

title: NEURO-TTR inotersen phase 2/3 - posted safety tables plus sponsor protocol chemistry section
identifier: NCT01737398 (sponsor protocol ISIS 420915-CS2); primary publication PMID 29972757
required_file: Posted results AE tables PLUS the 81-page Prot_000.pdf (section 2.3.2 Chemistry; Amendment 9 platelet-monitoring escalation with numeric stopping rules) PLUS SAP_001.pdf
gap_closed: Dual: human trial coagulopathy endpoints with exact denominators AND position-level chemistry for a clinically dosed, approved compound, taken from a primary sponsor document rather than reconstructed from a methods section
expected_yield: n=173 (inotersen 112, placebo 60); thrombocytopenia 14/112 vs 1/60; platelet count decreased 12/112 vs 0/60; serious thrombocytopenia 2/112; intracranial haemorrhage 1/112; GI haemorrhage 1/112; pulmonary embolism 1/112; embolic stroke 1/112; DVT 1/112 vs 1/60. Chemistry: 20-mer, all internucleoside linkages phosphorothioate, 5-nt 2'MOE wings each end, central 10-deoxynucleotide gap (5-10-5 MOE gapmer) complementary to a 20-nt stretch of the TTR 3'UTR
caution: The protocol gives the 5-10-5 ARCHITECTURE and the target region but NOT the base sequence - this is positional-by-pattern chemistry, not a literal per-residue string, so record the distinction. Amendment 9 escalated platelet monitoring (weekly, plus 6 weeks post-dose, with a >=30% fall stopping rule) after a severe thrombocytopenia case, which means AE rates are not comparable across pre- and post-amendment exposure periods.

title: Volanesorsen position-level chemistry via the APPROACH open-label-extension sponsor protocol
identifier: NCT02658175 (sponsor protocol ISIS 304801-CS7), protocol amendment 10 dated 2019-05-01
required_file: Prot_000.pdf section 2.3.2 Chemistry, plus sections 8.5.2 (Safety Monitoring for Platelet Count Results) and 8.5.3 (Safety Monitoring for Minor Bleeding Events) - a 1,327-page document, so target the sections
gap_closed: Position-level chemistry AND exact target coordinates for volanesorsen, the dataset's heaviest thrombocytopenia-signal compound, from an openly downloadable primary sponsor document. It is also the documented workaround for APPROACH (NCT02211209) having no posted protocol or SAP
expected_yield: 1 compound fully specified: synthetic 20-mer, all linkages phosphorothioate, 5-nt 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) ribonucleotide wings at both 5' and 3' ends, DNA gap between, complementary to apoC-III mRNA 3'UTR base positions 489-508; plus numeric platelet-count and bleeding monitoring thresholds
caution: Architecture and target coordinates, NOT a printed base sequence. This is a CS7 open-label-extension document being used as the chemistry source for the CS6 compound - the molecule is the same, but do not attribute CS7 protocol text to the APPROACH trial record. The same protocol-attachment pattern reportedly works on BROADEN (NCT02527343, ISIS 304801-CS17).

title: Olezarsen position-level chemistry via the Balance sponsor protocol - matched conjugated/unconjugated pair with volanesorsen
identifier: NCT04568434 (sponsor protocol ISIS 678354-CS3, Balance), protocol amendment 9 dated 2023-08-02

expected_yield: 1 compound fully specified: synthetic 20-mer, all linkages phosphorothioate, 5'-trishexylamino-(THA)-C6-GalNAc3 endcap, 5-nt 2'MOE wings both ends, four-region structure, complementary to apoC-III mRNA positions 489-508; plus n=66 posted safety results. The same Prot_SAP pattern is available on NCT05355402, NCT03385239, NCT02175004, NCT03728634, NCT04136184, NCT04307381 and NCT04030598

title: CTD/MeSH systematic-name harvest - full sequence and uniform-PS backbone for four clinically dosed first-generation oligonucleotides
identifier: MESH:C408162 (oblimersen/G3139); MESH:C502518 (edifoligide); MESH:C099587 (ISIS 5132/CGP 69846A); MESH:C525712 (trabedersen/AP 12009) - 4 records, one acquisition action
required_file: The four CTD chemical detail pages, or equivalently the MeSH SCR systematic-name strings from the CTD bulk chemical vocabulary report (machine-readable)
gap_closed: Raises the position-level-chemistry count for clinically dosed compounds at near-zero cost, in exactly the structural class most implicated in contact-pathway aPTT prolongation - uniform-PS first-generation oligos. Includes the only duplex in the set with BOTH strands fully specified
expected_yield: 4 compounds fully specified: oblimersen 18-mer all-2'-deoxy uniform PS (the heptadecasodium/17 Na+ salt independently confirms all 17 linkages are PS); edifoligide two 14-mers each all-deoxy uniform PS annealed 1:1; ISIS 5132 20-mer all-deoxy uniform PS; trabedersen 18-mer all-deoxy uniform PS. Human exposure is large - oblimersen dosed in thousands across phase 1-3, edifoligide in over 2,000 (PREVENT III/IV)
caution: These are controlled-vocabulary IDENTITY records, not study records - they supply ZERO coagulation observations, and CTD curates no gene, disease or phenotype rows at all for three of the four. Verify each systematic name against a primary source before treating it as the drug substance actually dosed: salt form, 5-methylcytosine content and any end modifications are not resolvable from a MeSH name. The value is that a curated vocabulary here is more complete than most primary publications, especially for the duplex.

title: Fesomersen RE-THINc ESRD phase 2 dose-ranging (GalNAc-conjugated FXI LICA)

expected_yield: n=307 across 4 arms (40 mg 77, 80 mg 79, 120 mg 76, placebo 75); thrombocytopenia dose gradient 3/77, 7/79, 7/76 vs 2/75; 13 coagulation-relevant serious AE terms each with per-arm denominators (AV fistula thrombosis 0/77, 1/79, 2/76, 3/75, plus vascular graft thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, subclavian vein thrombosis, peripheral artery thrombosis, superficial vein thrombosis, duodenal ulcer and GI/small-intestinal haemorrhage); primary endpoint as major plus clinically-relevant non-major bleeding per 100 person-years by arm

Same compound as entry 26 in a different population: do not double-count the compound. The placebo thrombocytopenia rate of 2/75 in an ESRD population shows the background rate is non-zero, so arm differences must be read against it.

title: Factor XI antisense oligonucleotide for prevention of venous thrombosis - SUPPLEMENTARY APPENDIX ONLY
identifier: PMID 25482425; PMC4367537; DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1405760 (NEJM 2015) (= OpenAlex W2102719739 = BioStudies S-EPMC4367537)

expected_yield: n=300 appendix tables; FXI activity and aPTT distributions, adjudicated VTE and bleeding detail. Exact table inventory UNKNOWN until opened

Acquire the SUPPLEMENT only and do not re-enter the main text. Note the on-target/off-target distinction: FXI reduction with aPTT prolongation is the intended pharmacology here, not PS contact-pathway toxicity, and conflating the two would corrupt the dataset. Pairs one-to-one with entry 24 on the identical construct.

title: Inhibition of coagulation by a phosphorothioate oligonucleotide (Henry et al. 1997) - RECLASSIFIED AS ANIMAL, NOT HUMAN
identifier: PMID 9361909; DOI 10.1089/oli.1.1997.7.503 (Antisense Nucleic Acid Drug Dev 1997); Henry SP, Novotny W, Leeds J, Auletta C, Kornbrust DJ
required_file: Full-text PDF - closed access, no PMC deposit, not in Europe PMC full text
gap_closed: The animal vertex of the ISIS 2302 same-construct triangle, plus a backbone-chemistry contrast and a set of enzymatic negatives that constrain the mechanism
expected_yield: Cynomolgus in vivo aPTT and PT time course against plasma oligonucleotide concentration across infusion durations and doses, plus in vitro spiking of citrated blood from untreated monkeys; intrinsic pathway more sensitive than extrinsic; qualitative chemistry ranking PS >> phosphodiester and 2'-propoxy; chromogenic-substrate negatives for factor Xa, factor XIa and thrombin, with a positive concentration-dependent effect when fibrinogen is the thrombin substrate; mechanism independent of heparin's
found_via: PubMed + Semantic Scholar (the two resources classify it CONTRADICTORILY)
caution: VERIFIED CORRECTION - the Semantic Scholar record classifies this as 'Human plasma clotting assays in vitro'. That is WRONG. I retrieved the Europe PMC core record and read the abstract: the study is cynomolgus monkey in vivo PLUS citrated blood from untreated MONKEYS in vitro. The MeSH 'Humans' tag (present alongside 'Macaca fascicularis') is almost certainly what caused the misclassification. This record does NOT close the human in vitro gap and must not be filed as human evidence. It is also wrongly described elsewhere in the record set as 'the foundational human in vitro PS-oligo anticoagulation paper' and as 'the seed whose citation graph produced most of this list' - the graph-anchor role is real, the human attribution is not. Acquire as one bundle with entries 6 and 18, all ISIS 2302.

title: Pharmacokinetic properties of ISIS 2302 in healthy male volunteers (Glover et al. 1997)
identifier: PMID 9316823 (J Pharmacol Exp Ther 1997)
required_file: Full-text PDF
gap_closed: The human in vivo vertex of the ISIS 2302 triangle - a concentration-anchored human aPTT point that can be regressed against the purified-human-factor inhibition constants from entry 6 and the monkey exposure-response from entry 17, on one identical construct
expected_yield: Healthy male volunteers, single and multiple 2-hour IV infusions, 0.06-2.00 mg/kg; brief dose-related aPTT increases timed to Cmax, with Cmax linearly related to dose; clinically insignificant C3a rises at higher repeated doses while C5a, blood pressure and pulse were unaffected. Participant count UNKNOWN
caution: The aPTT increases are described as brief and clinically insignificant, so this is a small-effect human row - its value is the same-construct regression, not the effect size. No other compound in the record set offers this three-tier triangle (purified human factors, human volunteers, monkey), so the three entries should be acquired and entered together or not at all.

title: Characterization of interactions of chemically-modified therapeutic nucleic acids with plasma proteins by fluorescence polarization
identifier: S-EPMC6379706 / PMC6379706 (Nucleic Acids Research 2019)
required_file: Main text plus gky1260_supplemental_files.pdf (594,060 bytes)
gap_closed: The binding layer beneath PS-driven contact activation: dissociation constants of chemically-modified oligonucleotides (PS and 2'MOE classes) against individual human plasma proteins including coagulation-pathway proteins, with per-construct chemistry stated
expected_yield: UNKNOWN construct-by-protein matrix size; cell-free human plasma protein binding constants
caution: Cell-free binding only - there is no coagulation FUNCTION readout, so this supports mechanism and covariate construction rather than endpoint rows. It was the only record returned by two orthogonal BioStudies queries, which is weak evidence of relevance rather than strong evidence of importance. Verify that coagulation-pathway proteins are actually in the measured panel before ranking it this highly in a final ingest order.

title: Defibrotide in the human endotoxaemia model - exploratory trial with ex vivo ROTEM and thrombin-generation markers
identifier: NCT02876601 (Medical University of Vienna); protocol/SAP dated 2017-07-24
required_file: Posted results (primary endpoint prothrombin fragment F1+2; secondary endpoints thrombin-antithrombin complexes, ROTEM clotting time, ROTEM maximum lysis) plus Prot_SAP_000.pdf

expected_yield: n=20 across 4 arms (LPS+defibrotide 16, LPS+placebo 16, placebo+defibrotide 3, placebo+placebo 4); 4 posted endpoints with group-level medians (fold*h) and exact denominators

The endotoxaemia challenge deliberately perturbs the coagulation background, so these values are NOT comparable to resting-state human plasma assays and must be flagged as challenge-model data. Defibrotide again has no single sequence - encode as a mixture, consistent with entry 4.

required_file: Registry posted-results AE tables, Prot_000.pdf (2018-06-27, 82 pp) and SAP (2020-07-22). The journal article and its safety appendix remain behind the Lancet Haematol paywall

caution: Marked already_in_our_sources = FALSE in the source data, so this is a genuine addition. REJECT the Semantic Scholar 'legal open route': the Southampton eprints file (eprints.soton.ac.uk/477603) is named Fitusiran_003_ATLAS_INH, and ATLAS-INH is a DIFFERENT trial (NCT03417102, PMID 37003287, entry 22). Do not cite it as the ATLAS-A/B manuscript without opening and verifying which arm it contains. Prefer the registry artifacts, which are unambiguous. Confirmed negative: ATLAS-A/B is in neither PMC nor Europe PMC nor BioStudies, so stop searching those. The protocol's NHP homology statement is a CLAIM of homology, not a printed sequence.

identifier: NCT03417102 (sponsor protocol EFC14768 / ALN-AT3SC-003) + PMID 37003287 (Young et al.)

expected_yield: n=60 (fitusiran 41, bypassing agents on-demand 19); fibrin D-dimer increased 3/41 vs 0/19; prothrombin fragment 1.2 increased 3/41 vs 0/19; serious thrombosis 1/41; subclavian vein thrombosis 1/41 vs 0/19
